newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Klima to decide CA sale after Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: Klima to decide CA sale after Jan 10.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima said on Tuesday he would make a decision on the sale of privatisation candidate Creditanstalt-Bankverein "as soon as possible" after a January 10 deadline for updated bids expires.
"It will happen as soon as possible," he told reporters. He declined to be pinned down on an exact date for the decision, but added: "I take it for granted that it won't take ten days."
Klima last week extended the tender to January 10 from a previous deadline of December 16 to allow current bidders to improve their offers for the flagship bank.

Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky on Monday said in an interview with Austrian news agency APA that the bank must be sold to the highest bidder, believed to be "socialist" Bank Austria, in accordance with European Union law.
Bank Austria has bid 16.8 billion schillings ($1.5 billion) for the government's 70 percent voting stake in conservative stronghold Creditanstalt.

A rival consortium of bidders led by insurer EA-Generali has bid a total of 13.8 billion schillings for the state's 19.9 million shares in the bank and wants to sell about a quarter of those on the market at a premium, 60 percent of which would also go to the government's coffers.
The value of a third offer made by Austrian entrepreneur Karl Wlaschek has not been disclosed but is estimated around 15 billion schillings.

Vranitzky's Social Democrats (SPOe) back Bank Austria, controlled by the SPOe-dominated City of Vienna, while the conservative People's Party favour the consortium bid, which has led to a rift in the coalition government. ($ = 10.98 Austrian Schillings)
